english.title: Fail to comply with a request made by enforcement officer - Environmental Protection - (Single-use Vapes) (Wales)
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonable excuse, failed to comply with a requirement imposed in the exercise of an enforcement officers powers

(A)_[for the production of, or the furnishing of extracts from, documents under regulation 10(1)(f)]_
(B)_[to provide him such facilities and assistance as were necessary under regulation 10(1)(g)]_
(C)_[to provide her such facilities and assistance as were necessary under regulation 10(1)(g)]_
(D)_[to leave premises or part of them or anything in them undisturbed under regulation 10(1)(h)]_

of the Environmental Protection (Single-use Vapes) (Wales) Regulations 2024 in that **(..SPECIFY FAILURE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 5(1)(b) and (2) of the Environmental Protection (Single-use Vapes) (Wales) Regulations 2024.

english.notes:
(i) See regulation 6 for the defence of due diligence where it can be shown a person took all reasonable steps and exercised all due diligence to avoid committing the offence.
(ii) Initial offences are civil and include stop notices, fixed penalty fines or compliance notices, or enforcement undertakings. Failure to comply with enforcement undertakings can lead to a criminal proceeding being brought against the individual. Failure to comply with other notices means an individual is guilty of an offence and could be liable for an unlimited fine or a prison sentence. See the Schedule to the regulations for the imposition of civil sanctions.

other.penalty:
Summary: a fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale.

Time limits for prosecutions:
6 months.

For offences committed on or after 12th March 2015 the fine on summary conviction is unlimited, see section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012.
